name: What permits are required for a commercial remodel in Pasadena?

mainEntity.name: What permits are required for a commercial remodel in Pasadena, and when do you need them?
mainEntity.text: What permits are required for a commercial remodel in Pasadena, and when do you need them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Commercial remodeling in Pasadena usually requires permit review whenever the work affects structure, occupancy, accessibility, or building systems. That commonly includes interior wall changes, electrical upgrades, plumbing relocations, HVAC modifications, restroom changes, fire alarm or sprinkler work, and tenant improvement build-outs. Cosmetic-only work may be treated differently, but many projects still need approval depending on the scope. The safest approach is to define the project early and confirm whether the work is exempt or permit-required before demolition starts. Permit timing matters because plan check, corrections, and resubmittals can affect the schedule. For business owners, this is especially important when coordinating lease deadlines or opening dates. A contractor familiar with local permitting can help reduce delays by preparing complete drawings, scope descriptions, and trade coordination documents. If the building is older, accessibility and code upgrades may become part of the permit review even if they were not in the original plan.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most commercial remodels in Pasadena require building permits, and many also need trade permits for electrical, plumbing, mechanical, or fire-related work. Even tenant improvements that seem minor can trigger permit review if walls, occupancy, accessibility, or systems are affected. Plans and fees are typically submitted through the city permit process before work begins.
